reviews.text: Sound of Metal is thoughtful in its refusal to offer pat solutions for complex and changeable medical circumstances, and immersive without being exploitative, never suggesting that it represents any monolithic experience of disability.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: What the film gets so right is that it’s not about fixing your physical flaws, but fixing your interpretation of those flaws...
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Usually, mainstream films depict afflictions and impairments as things that need to be fixed to make the person’s life whole again. “Sound of Metal,” conversely, makes sure that the objectivity stays intact.
reviews.author: Paul Emmanuel Enicola

reviews.text: For anyone who has tried to cope with a disability, this film will resonate and speak volumes for you as it accurately depicts the shock of a life-altering condition. Bring the tissues, because Sound of Metal cuts deep.
reviews.author: Sarah Cortinaz

reviews.text: Paul Raci has a gift of allowing his fellow actors space that is rare, indeed. But when he is allowed by the script to have emotional moments, he damn near steals the limelight, which is saying quite a lot given his scene partners.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: Darius Marder has crafted an incredible debut built around loss and fear that never wallows or becomes sentimental.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: The final scene of silence will be one that we will be thinking about for a while.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is another proof that Riz Ahmed is turning into one of the finest actors of his generation.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: No film from 2020 grew on me more than Sound of Metal. It’s a film that I thoroughly enjoyed when I first saw it, and I’ve grown to absolutely love it as it refuses to leave my mind.
reviews.author: Brett Doze

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed does not put a single foot wrong...
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: rich in subtlety and nuance, when it could have been overbearing and melodramatic
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Resting at the #21 spot of my favorite films released in 2020, "Sound of Metal" is set to join the Criterion Collection with a series of brand-new materials that allow for a deeper look at the concept and creation of this emotional work.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed’s performance in Sound of Metal is a rare thing. He has a brooding intensity and vulnerability that rivals Brando and Penn.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The film’s tough-minded yet thoughtful story plows some heavy ground and asks challenging questions.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Sound of Metal's explorations of grief, acceptance and of progression are a rewarding experience and as we've all just spent the better part of a year learning to accept and adapt to change foisted upon us, the film's messages are additionally resonant.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Sound of Metal occasionally gets lost in the visual flourishes, but this is a small gripe when compared to a performance that reveals an actor hitting his stride as an artist.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a stirring character study about finding inner peace.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Spearheaded by a dynamite lead performance, this story of recovery and, more so, denial, reaches and aching honesty.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: The final act's quietly played emotional turmoil - in which Cooke really gets to spread her wings - is a triumph, building to an elegant and heart-warming finale.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: As inconsistent and inherently dubious as this aural gambit may be, it achieves a kind of blunt-force effectiveness in tandem with the earnest, wild-eyed performance by Ahmed.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a profound journey that we rarely see depicted in film.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: [A] film that delves into the internal struggle of a man and his new condition. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a must-see. Ahmed 100% deserved his 2021 Oscar-nomination for Best Actor.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: A powerful film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gianmarco Farfán

reviews.text: An elegy to punk rock, to deafness, and to the peace that can be found when we embrace life's quietest moments -the silence within ourselves.
reviews.author: L.A. Hawbaker

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is an astonishing accomplishment for both its long-nascent director and its British star, Riz Ahmed, for whom his turn as heavy metal drummer Ruben represents a career-best performance.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: It's a tour-de-force that requires real concentration to appreciate, the sort of concentration you'll find only in the cinema.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: What sets this apart from other films in the "bloke sobs in the bathtub, then punches a hole in the wall" personal anguish genre is how the deaf community is depicted.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Sound of Metal never does anything particularly unexpected or intricate with its storyline, but the technical aspects of its filmmaking - from the editing to the sound profile to the acting - are always impressive.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Putting us in Ruben's head strengthens the theme of loss of identity... and makes the character's hardships hit harder than a drummer on a snare.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: Raci's performance, along with the deaf actress Lauren Ridloff's, makes Sound of Metal work, placing it beyond Ruben's individual condition and his harsh reactions to it with Lou...
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is the voice, eyes, and soul of Sound of Metal. Words simply can't convey what his vacant looks can.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: ...a predominantly successful effort that confirms Ahmed's place as one of his generation's most promising up-and-coming actors.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A triumph in acting and sound design, with the former featuring Riz Ahmed's career-best performance as Ruben Stone.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: While the plot stumbles with an unevenly paced final act, Sound of Metal is nevertheless an astoundingly affective and emotionally resonating character piece that shines an inspirational light on the Deaf community
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: Ahmed pours himself into his role as a drummer rapidly losing his hearing and turns a pretty good movie into something close to great with a punishing performance...
reviews.author: Rob Harvilla

reviews.text: This is a film that fuses the farthest limits of its form to tell its story and remind viewers of both the fragility and adaptability of life.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: This isn't a film about heavy metal, and in some ways it isn't a film about deafness either. It's about self-knowledge, hard choices and being able to learn and change, even when all of it seems impossible.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is electric in Sound of Metal, a movie that proves just how vital and transformative sound design can be.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Yes, Sound of Metal is a film about loss, but ultimately it's a celebration of the spirit. It never misses a beat - make sure you do the same.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: A drama that's as visceral and hard-hitting as its protagonist's drum solos.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: Marder does away with the stigma attached to disabilities, choosing to represent them as differences rather than handicaps.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Simply put, you don't hear movies like this every day.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A drama that speaks volumes about dealing with the obstacles life can throw your way, and questions whether the point is to overcome these obstacles, or embrace them.
reviews.author: James Hanton

reviews.text: With a sensitive screenplay, superb sound production and a career-best turn from Riz Ahmed, it deserves every award coming its way.
reviews.author: Phil W. Bayles

reviews.text: A beautiful and powerful film, Riz Ahmed leads with a ferociously naked performance and his cast and crew surround and support him. The result is one of the best films in years. On every level this is a great work of art.
reviews.author: Sarah Cook

reviews.text: You'll come away from this utterly shaken and moved by it all.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Taking you through the emotional wringer and out the other side, Sound of Metal is a bold, exploratory portrait of identity loss and rebirth.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: ...a strong little indie with a great performance by Riz Ahmed...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: A film that deserves to be seen by the widest possible audience, reminding us of cinema's unique ability to challenge, entertain, uplift and unite.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Somebody, please, give Riz Ahmed a starring vehicle worthy of his talents.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: There's clever use of sound, pulling you in and out of Ruben's ears, which creates a disorientating effect that I assume is intended.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Despite its oversimplification of Deaf culture, Sound of Metal generally constructs positive and nuanced characters.
reviews.author: Elaine Cho

reviews.text: Ahmed's performance is a force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Darius Marder's film is just as much the story of an awakening - a man's learning to listen, and to value a certain kind of stillness - as it is about the surface-level crisis of being suddenly struck deaf.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: A beautifully argued parable about the need to go where life takes you, Darius Marder's debut thrives on the soul of Riz Ahmed and the bold creativity of sound designer Nicholas Becker.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Ahmed's performance clarifies the drama and delivers the meaning of Ruben's final epiphany. He gives the film energy and point.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: [W]hile the film embraces... redemption saga beats, Marder's impressionistic approach ensures they add a lot more depth to what could easily have become another rudimentary issue movie about an able-bodied individual learning to become a better person...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" functions as a powerful reminder for hearing people not to take life and its run-of-the-mill sounds for granted-coffee dripping, birdsong, wind, and talking on the phone.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Ahmed's performance was stellar, riveting and fully realized, but even in his most emotional moments, understated and real.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a startling [directorial] debut for Marder and allows Riz Ahmed to shine as a compelling leading man.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Ahmed is terrific in the part, making us feel for his plight as his world unravels. (Full Content Review for Parents - Profanity, Nude Drawings, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a unique and powerful film, not just because its message of resilience resonates but because it makes hearing viewers more aware of an element of cinema that they tend to take for granted.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" does shake out as the inspirational tale of a guy who realizes he has to learn to live in the world he's found himself in, but the insight is hard-won and earned. It feels specific and therefore universal.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Film director/co-writer Darius Marder, in his feature film debut, has thoroughly captured the world of heavy metal, the sounds of gradual loss and the realm of silence that propel the plot...
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: A remarkably accomplished debut; expect big things from Marder.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Subtitles in any English film can mean inclusion for a huge sector of society [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Sound of Metal prioritizes the emotional and physical reality of its subject above all else, combining an observational view of the deaf community with an immersive portrait of a man caught between loss and recovery.
reviews.author: Cassidy Olsen

reviews.text: An affecting story of hope, desperation, and the amorphous nature of addiction, Sound of Metal is without question one of the most beautiful films to release in the past year.
reviews.author: Toussaint Egan

reviews.text: It examines the vicissitudes of deafness with honesty and a truly meticulous performance from Riz Ahmed. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: With Oscar buzz surging for Riz Ahmed, the time is now to check out his virtuoso performance as a rock drummer facing deafness in a riveting, resonant film whose thrashing power and emotional gravity exert a grip that won't let go.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed's percussive performance as a heavy metal drummer losing his hearing is worth banging the drum for.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Considering its delicate treatment of its subject matter and the performance of Ahmed, it really is one of the few must-sees so far in 2020.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Ahmed's performance is beautifully rendered, as he expresses his character's alternating frustration and curiosity about his situation with subtlety rather than showy dramatics.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: A thoughtful, intelligent film with a great deal to say, Sound Of Metal is something special.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is essential viewing for anyone who considers themselves a fan of movies. With great acting, stellar technical aspects, and a message that's rarely illuminated in film, it's one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a compelling story with stellar performances and one of the most original sound design you've ever heard.
reviews.author: Jean Henegan

reviews.text: ...one of the best features I've seen lately, with one of the year's strongest male performances.
reviews.author: Steve Murray

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is specific in its setting, but ultimately is a story of accepting the curveballs life throws at you.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: With its thoughtful examination of the deaf community and its gripping soundscapes, [Sound of Metal] breathes new life into a conventional narrative, delivering a remarkably sensitive cinematic experience.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: There is a beautiful and breathtaking amount of compassion in Sound of Metal. A film that revolves around a man that must find a new purpose in life.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed stars in an aural, experiential film that creates its own esoteric audioscape.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: [Riz] Ahmed handles Ruben with both tender vulnerability and bulldozing assurance that teeters into complete loss of control.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Ahmed's an absolutely unstoppable performer, deep wells of discipline and commitment coming out in a performance of passionate intensity and wounded vulnerability.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: So much of the film rests on [Ahmed] selling you this man's experience with bare bones expressions. You get everything you need and then some.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Director Daris Marder excels here specifically because of his unique use of sound design to give us greater insight to our lead character.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: There's nothing louder in this film than Ahmed's blank expression. Sound of Metal lives on his face, and it is gorgeous.
reviews.author: Brad Gullickson

reviews.text: Paul Raci's performance is an apt use of that critical cliché, a 'revelation' ... [and] late in the film, a major international star makes an appearance that'll make your eyes pop wide open.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a stunning film-making accomplishment. It's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed's work in the lead role is a tremendous piece of screen acting, easily one of the best performances of the year.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is fantastic in this sometimes devastating drama that provides an insight into the struggles faced by the deaf community.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: That's the essential beauty of the narrative: the sound of metal may be elusive, but it's sharp, like a dagger to the soul.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Sound of Metal shows the millennium's avoidance of soulful self-examination. Merely a showy cinematic tattoo, a narcissistic desecration of the body, Sound of Metal is a work of spiritual vacancy.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: A listening experience that I haven't had anywhere else, though the filmmaking is great too.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: The production is done really well, and the performances stand out...it's a quiet, intimate film, but I kept waiting for it to hook me...good, but a bit at arms-length.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: While the performances are certainly strong (especially by Paul Raci as Ruben's mentor), the film's muddled politics undercut its emotional impact by refusing to embrace the ambiguity of its protagonist's plight.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a transcendent film that happens to be deeply grounded. It feels revolutionary, weaving a profound rhythm into its quietest moments.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: [An] emotional interpretation from Olivia Cooke. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Venero Torres

reviews.text: 'Sound of Metal' doesn't miss a beat.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: The only sense of emotional continuity that seems believable to me in the film is Ruben's emotional journey. That journey alone is enough for me to give this film a pass.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Losing your hearing can be hard, but when you are a musician, it can be career ending.
reviews.author: Brooke Daugherty

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed captures at its perfection the combination between despair and hope. The film stops being the story of a musician that loses his hearing and becomes the story of a rediscovered human being. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The film is startlingly artful for a directorial debut, and endlessly surprising.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: ... Marder grabs us, not so much with the vociferous metal music or any type of artistic pose, but rather with an effective sound design and narrative quality.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed leads this film about loss and addiction. The sound mixing and editing in the film was so incredible that it actually made me feel uncomfortable.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is a vibrant and mesmerizing catastrophe as he falls utterly to pieces.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: A purposefully-quiet film...
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: [Riz Ahmed] provides a sensitive performance, agitated although at no time excessive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Júlia Gaitano Mendizábal

reviews.text: A film so immersive that you will spend half of it anxiously and overwhelmed. A surprising Riz Ahmed in a role that will take at least the nomination for Best Actor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: First-time feature writer/director Darius Marder...does something remarkable in almost every scene of Sound of Metal, particularly when it comes to his use of sound.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Instead of a point of view, Sound of Metal gives us a point of hearing.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is a legit Oscar contender.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: What [director Darius] Marder, his writers, and his sound engineering team do is to make deafness one of the stars of their motion picture. How "Sound Of Metal" proceeds is certain to confound some and elevate others.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed delivers one of the most complex and moving on-screen transformations of the year.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Those behind the film intended you to watch this with the captioning on. Totally immersing hearing people into the world of deaf people. Want the sounds, etc. to really hit you and garner a visceral reaction.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: The pluses outweigh the minuses here, thanks to Ahmed's understated stoicism, how he modulates Ruben's resentment and pent-up anger.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Ruci is absolutely amazing and plays Joe with such honesty and pathos, which also comes from the script.
reviews.author: Jessica Mason

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a collectively disarming experience for everyone watching, and takes great pains to present the life of those with hearing impairments in a constructive way, without romanticizing.
reviews.author: Emma Stefansky

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a film with perfect narrative rhythm; the cinematic story makes interesting, poignant decisions for the entirety of its runtime.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: An inspiring journey of self-discovery, elevated by Ahmed's career-defining performance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a film well worth listening to and the benefit of viewing it from home is that you can watch with headphones on to fully appreciate the audio.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Without giving in to sentimentality, filmmaker Darius Marder recounts an emotionally raw story in a way that's deeply involving.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: the big star of the show here is Marder's startling and innovative sound techniques
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The sound design is such that I can't help but feel annoyed that I'm watching it in any setting other than one with an immersive, massive sound system.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: A genius of a film is that never goes anywhere expected, and the simple theme that we're all overcoming handicaps resonates like the echo of stillness. A rhythmic masterpiece!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Although writer/director Darius Marder's character study is a nuanced, thoughtful, surprisingly delicate exploration of the horrifying recalibrations life often demands of us, my goodness are just there so many ways in which it could have sucked.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is so incredibly satisfying. Everything around us is just an obnoxious and noisy cacophony. The world's most beautiful symphony is utter and complete silence. Brilliantly acted with a powerful message that leaves a colossal impact.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: Anchored by an award-worthy performance from Riz Ahmed, this is a powerful drama that immerses the audience in its lead character's world as well as any film in recent memory. It is one of 2020's best films.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: This film is often painful to watch; it's also deeply moving, thanks to a couple of killer performances.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Honest, poignant, authentic and emotionally gripping, Sound of Metal turns out to be one of the best dramas I've seen in 2020. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" isn't a feel-good film by any stretch; it is at times incredibly bleak...However, between the compelling story, the outstanding lead performance and the unforgettably innovative sound work, it is certainly touched by greatness.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Featuring a strong performance by Riz Ahmed, the various sound techniques used to emulate hearing loss and recovery, lift the already effective story about coping with illness and even tragedy
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: While this film, on paper, may appear to exude the sentimentality of a sports film defined by its protagonist injuring themselves, Sound of Metal avoids schmaltz and instead, cuts straight to the heart.
reviews.author: Maria Sherman

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed gives a standout performance in this moving film.
reviews.author: Audra Schroeder

reviews.text: What do we owe ourselves, and how do we fail ourselves? The challenges of those reckonings are the core of Sound of Metal, a film whose technical achievements mirror the quality of its emotional truths.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a beautifully intimate portrait with Ahmed leading the charge... It's a raw, intimate look into one man's struggle with acceptance. A grappling of drastic change.
reviews.author: Melody McCune

reviews.text: A truly astounding debut from Darius Marder, Sound of Metal is the kind of achingly honest and impactful film that will stay with you for months (and probably years) after you've seen it, and we mean that in the best way possible.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is not always easy viewing, but provides a nuanced, hard-hitting character study that enlightens, sobers, and leaves a lasting impact.
reviews.author: Alex McPherson

reviews.text: The sound design and lead performance are so good that it's easy to overlook its spotty screenplay and pedestrian filmmaking.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a stunner. It's one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: This is an incredibly powerful and impactful film!
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: A deeply humane, must-see film.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Pairing a career best performance from Riz Ahmed with Nicolas Becker's groundbreaking sound design results in a truly immersive experience.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Sound of Metal operates as a compassionate character piece enhanced through its brazen artistic drive.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: There is a breathless sonic majesty to Darius Marder's superb Sound of Metal that left me a discombobulated mess long after the drama had ended.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A superb first feature from Darius Marder. And possibly the best drama about a drummer since Whiplash. [Full review in spanish].
reviews.author: Julio Fernando Navas

reviews.text: A film that is a surprisingly hard watch, but also essential viewing...how often does a movie make your whole body feel invested, suffocated, and finally - cathartically - floating?
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: For a movie that doesn't say much, the message within "Sound of Metal" is loud and clear.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: It's the kind of indie drama that will linger because it's a quiet joy - self-consciously so - anchored by one of the year's most remarkable lead performances.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Sound of Metal may fly under the radar but will be one of the best movies you'll see this year and you'll be glad you gave it a chance.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Ahmed simply must get an Oscar nomination. It's a beautiful tale about recovery and moving forward.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: As the pacing of the film revs up, it readies us for the finale -- one that will leave you speechless and contemplative. It's not often a film can provide these elements along with a natural sense of empathy.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" is furious, unsentimental and brilliant at putting the viewer literally inside Ruben's head.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Ahmed and Raci are standouts, with Cooke providing powerful emotional support. The film's sound design is especially important here, as what is heard and how it is perceived plays an important role in putting us in Ruben's shoes.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: 'Sound of Metal' resonates with Ahmed's Oscar-worthy performance.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: The movie may be stylized, but it's not ostentatious. Its universe feels lived-in and authentic...
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed delivers a solid performance as Ruben, a heavy metal drummer dealing with hearing loss in this otherwise pedestrian therapy drama.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: ... takes a bold approach in terms of its overall artistic design and sound design; you are almost always experiencing the world as Ruben experiences it.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: There is sentiment here, but no sentimentality, no reaching for unearned emotion, no need to couch Ruben as a subject of our condescending pity, or blanket praise.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: It's an impressive, bordering on dazzling, film in its skill and command of the viewer.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Paul Raci is a bastion of wisdom that stirs you through an ever attentive and patient gaze;It's an honest performance that brings emotion to the story.[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: The film immerses us in Ruben's predicament completely. Protagonists in films rarely come as relatable as this.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Ahmed lets us into his character's mind as we understand the demons with which he struggles and his intrinsic conflicts.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" leaves an impression that echoes long after it's over.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: it sees its characters as people, not just as symbols, and invests all of them with such humanity that we actually do care what happens to them.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: There isn't a phony note in the entirety of Sound of Metal, making it one of the most lyrical, gripping and best films of 2020.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: ASMR fans, this is for you. Discovering the sound of silence never felt so expansive.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is an above-average addiction drama, and Riz Ahmed is blazingly good as Ruben.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Masterfully acted and directed. The best film of the year.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Watching [Riz] Ahmed flourish without words, typically an actor's lifeline, is a joy. It's a massive challenge and he rises to it with aplomb.
reviews.author: Joey Keogh

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is an actor with a fierce knowledge of how to occupy a character, how to live inside them and make them breathe. Whomever he is in the moment, we believe him.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: For the most part, the heavy lifting of the film is left to Ahmed, and he handles it effortlessly, in a moving and unforced turn that, while characterized by moments of rage and destruction, is ultimately a journey of acceptance.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Compelling film where Riz Ahmed delivers a quietly powerful performance as a heroin-addicted drummer in a Metal band who is going deaf.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: [Riz Ahmed] gives one of the best performances of the year thus far.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Sound of Metal will leave you stunned. There hasn't been anything quite like it, and considering its independent nature, that's even more of an achievement.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a phenomenal film...
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: It's Ahmed's movie, really, the kind of all-in performance necessary to elevate a film like this to more than it might have been otherwise.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: With phenomenal sound design and an emotional performance from Ahmed, "Sound of Metal" is a profound story worth putting at the top of your watchlist this year.
reviews.author: Hannah Hoolihan

reviews.text: The movie's a little sketchy and underwritten, and it feels sometimes as if scenes have been pared away or cut altogether to concentrate on Ahmed. But Ahmed really is terrific.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Sound of Metal tells a story about coping and overcoming while avoiding the narrative pitfall of artifice.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a film specially made for people who can't hear... That's not the only way in which this film is remarkable, either.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Speaking of stillness and silence, there is a tremendous weight of heart and profundity found in the difference between those two states in this film.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: A fascinating story told in an entertaining way and highlighted by a brilliant acting performance by Riz Ahmed
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: I assure you the time won't be wasted. This is high-caliber filmmaking, and its genesis is the sound design in this film. It's the epitome of innovation.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Marder employs masterful sound design, lacing the soundtrack with distorted sounds and ringing ears to fully immerse us in the deaf drummer's shoes. Few films make better use of silence.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Darius Marder's directorial debut is a little loose around the edges, but the vision is intact even if the emotion, alluded to in the trailer, isn't always present.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is an innovative piece of work; it starts off intense and visceral until it takes a turn and becomes a tender, compassionate exploration of acceptance.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" understands the gift that is hearing and the blessings of silence alike.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: [T]he film is an intensely unique sonic experience that demands careful and focused aural attention.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Like the best works of art, Darius Marder's riveting drama feels both of-the-moment and absolutely timeless. It's about freefall. And grief. Redefining what you thought was normal. Then learning how to accept it.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: At the end of the day, this is an expertly crafted labor of love championing the abandonment of dreams. What's the sound of one hand clapping?
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: The powerful new "Sound of Metal"... works because it's really about characters and politics, emotions and empathy.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Sound of Metal perfectly depicts a health crisis, one so severe (except for death) that life has to change in every imaginable sense.
reviews.author: Sarah Ksiazek

reviews.text: An inmersive experience thanks to Riz Ahmed's phenomenal performance, solid direction and great sound design. A really touching film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: One of the most profound and needed films, Sound of Metal is the perfect place to let Riz Ahmed showcase his ability
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: The observant film is memorable for showing us how rewarding and lyrical silence can be.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: An engrossing deeply affecting, meticulously crafted movie. The tone is straightforward and naturalistic. The camera focuses on intimate connections between the characters. This is a thoughtful, grounded, human scale film.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: With a credible sincerity (and jaw-dropping sound design), Sound of Metal gives a realistic and poignant look at deaf culture in America.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Beginning at a high decibel level and ending sotto voce, Marder's film takes us on an alternately searing and poignant emotional journey.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: One of the film's best features is its refusal to indulge in triumph-of-the-human-spirit clichés that so often weigh down disability narratives.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: As Ruben's fear and rage begins to open itself to the unknown, the movie reaches toward something profound - finding real, furious power in the spaces between the sound.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" is a well-made, empathetic and heart-wrenching cautionary tale.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" isn't a movie about wallowing in pity and self-destructive behavior. It's a mature depiction of a tender soul forced to find a way forward.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: It's the magnificent Riz Ahmed in one of the year's most truly electric performances, with great support, literally and figuratively, from Olivia Cooke.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: With 'Sound of Metal,' filmmaker Darius Marder crafts one of the most compelling, raw, and unforgettable films of the year.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: An engulfing sensory experience, Sound of Metal is an astonishing work that only gets richer on repeat viewings.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: It has the best sound design that I've heard in any movie this year... They use sound in such an interesting and immersive way.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Vivid and insightful ... not many movies have explored the day-to-day experience of deafness with this level of compassion or sincerity.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a great example of how losing the ability to hear doesn't make anyone less of a person ... The movie's outstanding sound editing and sound mixing completely immerse viewers into the experience ... [with] superb acting.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: You can hear every ache in the sound of silence.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: One of the great out-of-nowhere performances of the year.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Viewers can decide what they might do in the drummer's shoes. It's a fascinating, frightening what-if.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Raci's Joe doesn't view deafness as a disability but as a gateway to different forms of communication. Director Darius Marder creates a sound design that frequently mirrors Rubin's perspective.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: [Marder] keeps us interested even though, frankly, Sound of Metal needn't be quite such a one-man show, and even Ruben isn't fully dimensionalized in the script.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Ahmed learned both American Sign Language and drumming to play the part, and he's convincing. It's an eye-opening film.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: Ahmed, Cooke, and Raci all give understated, natural performances that draw us into the story even more than the immersive sound design.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed's mind-bogglingly great.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: A movie that doesn't just allow for silence but thrives in it, with Ahmed's eyes and body language charting the arc of his character.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: British actor and rapper Riz Ahmed absolutely shines as Ruben Stone, an American punk-metal drummer whose life is upended when he abruptly loses his hearing while on tour.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a poignant study of trying to accept the life one has been given and not dwelling on the loss.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The film is profound, frightening, uplifting and, yes, actually breathtaking at times, and you're not likely to take your hearing for granted anytime soon afterward.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: What keeps Sound Of Metal from wandering off into the wilderness is Ahmed's performance, which remains compelling even when the script loses its narrative footing.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: It's conventional, but it also breaks ground: Angsty addiction dramas may be overrepresented in the movies, but sensitive, lived-in portraits of Deaf culture and community have always been in short supply.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There are multiple paths that this story could have taken, but the Marders have found an unlikely, unique, and rewarding one...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Marder's script juggles the drama and tensions throughout this story with a sense of reality but seldom actually resorts to melodrama for cheap effect. Sound of Metal will stick with you and is easily among the year's best.
reviews.author: Spencer Perry

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" is an act of empathy, and like a lot of empathy, it does not come easily.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Yes, this is Riz Ahmed's showcase and his ultimate moment, thus far. But, excellent performances abound.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: While [Sound of Metal] fails as a game-changer and a (r)evolution of cinematic sonics, it works somewhat better as a bit of affectingly lived-in, post-shtick drama.
reviews.author: Luke Gorham

reviews.text: It not only features some of the best work of Riz Ahmed's young career, but instantly establishes Darius Marder as a filmmaker to keep an exceptionally close eye on.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Come for the redemptive story; stay for the sound design.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: There's plenty to praise, but what a terrific showcase Sound of Metal is for Riz Ahmed.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Sound of Metal doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it does make a pretty darned spectacular wheel.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Propelled by a distinctive style and a potent lead performance, Darius Marder's "Sound of Metal" builds a singular tension between silence and noise.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is the definition of unforgettable and original.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Bolstered by an amazing, understated performance by Riz Ahmed, Sound of Metal skillfully avoids phony melodrama in order to tap into some essential human truths, and is one of the year's very best films.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: There's no question in my mind that Sound of Metal and particularly Ahmed and some of Marder's crew will be in serious talks for awards in the new year.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The journey Ruben takes from recovering addict to a man at peace with himself largely fails to convince, the gaps in the storytelling too obvious to pick apart.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: "Sound of Metal" has restlessness and definite opinions on technology, and when Marder taps into the pure behavior of personal growth, he makes a hypnotic film.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The standout film of the year and a masterpiece in inclusive, thoughtful filmmaking. An emotional story that's backed by an incredible cast, with an enthralling performance by Ahmed. Even more, it's a transformative experience for you as a viewer.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: The film thrives in authenticity. Riz Ahmed and Olivia Cooke are first-rate but the film's true gem is actor-musician Paul Raci who was born to play his role.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Brought to life with a tour-de-force performance from Riz Ahmed and transportive sound design fashioned to trap viewers in the muffled soundscape of its protagonist.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: While "Sound of Metal" doesn't venture to unexpected places, director Darius Marder - working from a script based on a story by "Blue Valentine" director Derek Cianfrance - keeps it all rooted in a heartfelt reality.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: This film not only sports two fine performances, but does absolutely amazing things with sound design.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It's about adapting to one's environment or wallowing in psychological pain. Sound of Metal is a tearjerker regardless, but anyone that can relate on a more personal level is going to be as wrecked as Ruben's ears
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Director Darius Marder and his cast and crew help bring understanding about deafness to those who can hear. That is a tough task and they do it well.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Ahmed doesn't engage in histrionics, instead giving a quiet, internal performance...The man we are left with (in a knockout of a final scene) is very changed from the one we first met.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a great portrayal of deafness in film using smart sound design and a stellar performance by Riz Ahmed to communicate the experience. And while it loses steam as it makes its way to the finale the core message is powerful and poignant.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Documentary and music video camera genius Daniël Bouquet combines his two interests to give the film a naturalistic, almost fly-on-the-wall feel, but everything is really in service of the sound design.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It's an extremely well-structured and consistently interesting debut film, never wasting too much time on any particular plot point and concluding with the only possible appropriate ending for this story.
reviews.author: Reuben Baron

reviews.text: Beautifully applies the talents of one of the best actors working today.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a sweet, melancholy character study about a deeply flawed man learning to cope with personal tragedy.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: An acting tour-de-force by Ahmed and the film's sound design is also worthy of the praise it has been getting. A brilliant depiction of a man whose life capsizes overnight and must gradually adjust to a new reality.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: Beautifully produced and directed with an abundance of clarity, Sound of Metal is made to make us care by design-its trick is in how it pulls us along to experience all of the ups and downs with our leading man, wringing us all out by the film's end.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: Darius Marder's film captures, with urgency and tenderness, just how enticing the residue of the past can be.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Wholly committed, uninhibited, and emotionally charged, [Riz] Ahmed's performance in Sound of Metal elevates an already astonishing film to a higher, more perceptive level.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: At its most basic level, Sound of Metal will make you reevaluate and cherish your five senses, without which this vivid world would dim and perhaps cease to exist. But Marder delves much deeper.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed and Olivia Cooke sizzle in this story about a rock drummer dealing with sudden deafness. Kudos to Darius Marder for bringing dignity and education to screen about this world of slience.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Marder's screenplay and direction are both tender and textured, asking the question of what it would take to force you to change your life. And when that change is offered, would you even accept it?
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: The sound design accompanying Sound of Metal is among the most exquisite to accompany any film in 2020.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Marder's use of silence and sound is truly extraordinary and goes a long way in putting us in Ruben's disoriented state of mind.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Cemented by an impeccable performance from the immense talent that is Riz Ahmed, this is a deeply earnest depiction of the chaotic journey when everything you know is ripped away.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: As Ruben, a drummer that loses his ability to hear, Ahmed is a complete powerhouse.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: This is a very stylish film that trusts in how much we want to watch Riz Ahmed walk around, which turns out to be a lot.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed is doing particularly amazing work in this very, very good film.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: Sometimes the silence is a loud scream. A great film about how we accept or not our changes in life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: In a powerful story of a musician losing his hearing, Riz Ahmed turns in a spectacular performance that overcame my fears of disability appropriation.
reviews.author: Michael McNeely

reviews.text: A truly interesting, clever, and original movie. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: It's a devastating, poignant, and ultimately hopeful film, especially for a side of humanity that rarely sees itself portrayed on screen.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: It's not only thanks to [Darius] Marder's direction, but [Riz] Ahmed's passionate intensity, that Sound of Metal succeeds in its own right.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Marder hasn't filled in the dramatic interior of what does happen. He has made a movie about deafness that's at once experiential and too muffled to hear.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Boasting a solid story about profound loss, a knockout performance by [Riz] Ahmed, and award-worthy sound design, Sound of Metal cuts through the clutter.
reviews.author: Joi Childs

reviews.text: Sound of Metal is a thoughtful examination of the deaf community, and an innovative production of sound design.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: The film provides a moving portrait of how people can make the choice to treat their disability as an enhancement, not an impairment, to their experience of life.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: [There's] honesty in revealing how saviors aren't beholden to their saved. Love is transformative and what we needed to survive then isn't what we need to keep surviving now.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: It's a curious confection and not one destined to have much of a commercial life - a shame, because Ahmed is on top form.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: The assaultive, near-experimental sound design goes a long way towards putting us in Ruben's head, but Ahmed's performance makes us understand his character with a clarity that eludes Ruben himself.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Ahmed is superb in this impactful drama which explores attitudes towards and questions about disability.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed has never been better than in this extraordinary experiment in sound design. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: A heartfelt and sad look at learning to love one's self after struggle, and finding hope and serenity even after the worst hard times...
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Sound of Metal injects visceral, edgy circumstances with remarkable sensitivity.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed gives the best performance of his career.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Sound of Metal might be working from an old playbook, but it finds new ways to liven it up.
reviews.author: Vikram Murthi

reviews.text: Marder proves himself a natural cinematic storyteller but Sound of Metal is built in a such a way that it is dependent on the skill of its cast. Luckily, they come through beautifully (suggesting that Marder is a damn good director of actors as well).
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Marder's film about loss and codependency is the most distinctive debut by a filmmaker this year.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: But even when the cultural politics are explicit, Ahmed's performance and a sure-footed script by Marder and his brother Abraham ensure that this remains one man's story - and one that should be warmly welcomed at arthouses.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: Riz Ahmed gives the best performance of his career in Darius Marder's powerful story about a drummer losing his hearing.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: There's an a-ha moment upon learning that Marder's a close collaborator of Derek Cianfrance; this feels at times like "Blue Valentine" painted black.
reviews.author: Charles Barfield

synopsis: During a series of adrenaline-fueled one-night gigs, itinerant punk-metal drummer Ruben (Riz Ahmed) begins to experience intermittent hearing loss. When a specialist tells him his condition will rapidly worsen, he thinks his music career — and with it his life — is over. His bandmate and girlfriend Lou (Olivia Cooke) checks the recovering heroin addict into a secluded sober house for the deaf in hopes it will prevent a relapse and help him learn to adapt to his new situation. But after being welcomed into a community that accepts him just as he is, Ruben has to choose between his equilibrium and the drive to reclaim the life he once knew. Utilizing startling, innovative sound design techniques, director Darius Marder takes audiences inside Ruben’s experience to vividly recreate his journey into a rarely examined world.
